title: Add plan/critic convention for content mirroring a governing source
summary: Planner prompt requires a plan that writes content summarising or mirroring a governing source (term definitions, cache keys, seeded records) to name the source and list every dependent place (each term mention, each compiled-in file). The critic prompt rejects plans without it. A fixture plan missing the list is shown rejected, and CHANGELOG gets an entry. Audience: Athena's planner and critic stages, and maintainers judging failure class f62n.

defaults_applied.how: Fixture test for the rejection; cargo test and clippy must pass.
fmt, clippy and test criteria run by the verifier.
Rule enforced by a tested plan check where possible, with the critic prompt as backup.
Criterion checks a plan missing the list is rejected.
Prompt edits plus one fixture test and a CHANGELOG entry.
Prompt and changelog wording is plain and self-contained.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md and critic.md (plain prompts, 966 and 902 of 1300 tokens, so about 334 and 398 left), crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs (dependents_findings, the shape check run on plans at line ~310, with unit tests) and crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs. No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are not touched.

Reading: a prompt convention plus a test. Planner prompt gains a rule (name the source, list every dependent place, and require one criterion comparing written content to that list). Critic prompt gains a rule to raise a major finding (verdict revise or reject) when it is missing. The fixture test is an admission-level plan fixture without the list, asserted to yield a major finding. If a prompt-only critic rule cannot be tested deterministically, the check is an admission.rs shape rule, which is the assumption I take.
The existing `dependents` section and its shape check are the model; the new list is a separate plan section or an extension of it, the producer's design choice, kept small.
Failure-class record records/failure-classes/2026-10/20261017-182305-f62n.json is a reference and is not modified; records/ never changes.
athena.toml and defaults.toml need no change; the planner and critic prompt token budgets must not be exceeded.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md states that a job writing content that summarises or mirrors a governing source must name the source and list every place in it the content depends on (every mention of a term, every compiled-in file for a cache key), and must have at least one criterion comparing the written content to that list, not just its structure.

crates/athena-context/prompts/critic.md instructs the critic to reject (major finding) a plan that writes such mirrored content without the named source and complete list, or without a comparing criterion.
A test with a plan fixture that lacks the source list is rejected (a major finding or refusal naming the missing list), while the same fixture with the list is accepted; check with `cargo test`.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the convention, citing failure class f62n.
Prompt sets stay within their token budgets (planner 1300, critic 1300), shown by the existing prompt budget test in `cargo test`.
No unrelated behavior changes: `cargo test` passes including existing tests, `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Editing records/ including the f62n failure-class record or the four introspections
Changes to reader, producer or verifier prompts
departures: Hard-rated job touching the plan critic gate and a tight prompt token budget make the verification pass slightly less likely than the reference.
hard_reason: It changes the rule the critic uses to reject plans, which is part of the run pipeline's planning gate.
